content:
If you've spent the entire summer testing apps on the Apple Watch beta, you may have noticed some existing apps failing to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is now automatically updating these apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

These updates will be pushed via the App Store, with version release notes stating: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features have been added."

Apple notified developers this week that the entire process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems, is expected to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates are arriving just in time before the launch.

Apple explained that this arrangement is necessary because some watchOS apps encountered issues on the arm64 architecture. Reports indicate they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning properly without requiring any action from developers.
